subject.title: Feature: Private Mode for demos and content creation

question: What privacy guarantee should OpenClaw make for Private/Secret/Incognito sessions across protocol, persistence, memory/plugins, channels, diagnostics, and UI?
rationale: Automation can identify the missing enforcement surfaces, but only maintainers can choose the security boundary, supported metadata retention, activation semantics, and upgrade-compatible API shape.

options.title: Design a cross-layer private session contract
options.body: Add an explicit private/ephemeral session marker and require every durable context, memory, transcript, plugin, channel, diagnostics, and UI path to honor it before exposing the mode.

options.title: Limit scope to context suppression
options.body: Expose a narrower demo-only mode that disables bootstrap/context injection but does not promise no persistence, with UI copy that avoids a privacy guarantee.

options.title: Defer until session storage redesign
options.body: Keep the issue open but block implementation until the broader session/transcript persistence architecture can support an enforceable no-write mode cleanly.

recommendation.title: Design a cross-layer private session contract
recommendation.body: Add an explicit private/ephemeral session marker and require every durable context, memory, transcript, plugin, channel, diagnostics, and UI path to honor it before exposing the mode.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame and the prior review both point to steipete as the most visible recent session/privacy routing owner for this decision.
